title: The guardrail that fails open
blurb: The classifier timed out and the draft allowed the prompt through.
prompt: During a classifier outage the guardrail allowed everything, and the review queue missed blocks because the violation events were fire-and-forget. The model-generated draft returns allow on any exception and publishes violations with no outbox. Review it, fix it, and prove the gate fails safe and loses no violation.
aiNote: The draft maps every classifier exception and timeout to allow, so an outage silently disables the gate instead of failing safe, and it publishes violation events without an outbox so a broker rejection loses the block record.
testIdea: Kill the classifier stub and assert high-risk tenants get the conservative deny while low-risk tenants use their configured fallback; reject the produce and assert an outbox row exists; replay the queue and assert no duplicate review entries.
followUps: Which tenants should fail closed and which should fail open, and who decides?
How would you version a rule set so a rollback cannot resurrect a retracted rule?
What goes in the span offsets so reviewers can find the exact offending phrase?
